description: Welcome to the latest collection of adventures with everyone’s favourite golden family! Bart’s pranking all of Springfield once again, Ralph attempts to survive in the wilderness, Homer has a new invention, and Lisa hosts a geeky board game evening!

Welcome back to the sizzlingly exciting adventures of the Simpsons! In this issue, Homer takes Bart fishing in the deep blue sea, Sideshow Bob gets even, Bart gets lost at the zoo, and Springfield’s prankster’s face gets stuck!

Welcome to the Bart special! Now, everyone! Do the Bartman! In this special issue, enjoy NINE hilarious stories of springfield’s most infamous prankster! Known throughout springfield as Bartman, El Barto, and “Why you little-“!

Welcome to Issue #26! Last issue was bursting with Bart, but now it’s time for Homer’s epic tales! Brace yourself for Homer the brainiac, stand by for Homer the reality TV star and keep reading for Homer the… criminal?!

Welcome to Simpsons Comics #27! In this issue, Marge becomes Roller Derby Queen with the Springfield Spitfires, and then takes a peek behind the curtains in Ogdenville. Bart, Lisa and Maggie team up to fight crime in Springfield, and Homer takes laziness to a whole new level!

You have stepped into Simpsons Comics #28! Watch your step, there are doughnut crumbs everywhere. In this issue, discover if Lisa really is a Simpson! Marge sees the funny side with her new Life Coach, Krusty The Clown! Last (and definitely least) is Moe. Will he find true love?

It’s the biggest crossover event in history! In this issue, worlds collide as the Planet Express crew are trapped in Springfield! Then, Dr. Hibbert warns against the dangers of videogames, Marge’s detective skills are put to the test and Santa’s Little Helper proves that every dog has its day – or night!

Can you believe it? It’s issue 30! In this book, we’re bringing you three comics that are more jam-filled than a year’s supply of donuts, more juicy than the perfect turkey sandwich, and with more twists and turns than a murder on an oriental rollercoaster!

Drawn in front of a live studio audience, it’s Simpsons #31! Hold your applause, please, or else you might drop this book! In this issue, the Simpson family visits a wretched hive of scum and villainy: a comic convention! Then, Homer opens a comic store! Finally, an adventure in 25 hours of less!

Note: results may vary depending on reading speed.

Brush off that rain, warm up your hot beverage of choice and curl up with the funniest magazine on this newsstand: it’s Simpsons #32! In this issue, Homer gets trapped in a world without Duff! Then, not naming any obvious names, SOMEONE broke the internet! Also, Homer teaches American history, and Dr. Nick Riviera gives medical advice! (Is it still advice if it isn’t accurate?)

Hey-hey reader! In this international issue, the Simpson Family head around the world in twenty-eight pages. Homer must get creative as he endeavours to entertain Springfield and protect his rubbish from a rabid raccoon. Then, a completely-deadly and totally-not-harmless super-villain returns to Springfield!

Welcome to issue 34! This issue’s got it all: hysterical history – all completely true and fact checked on Wikipedia – a sugary smuggling ring, a revolt against a celebrity chef, and a comatose clown with a case of identity theft! What are you waiting for?

Ka-Pow! Welcome to issue 35 of the Simpsons Comics! In this issue, we’ve got the most ambitious crossover in comics history as CSI: Springfield shares pages with Springfield School for Lonely Adults, while Bartman, the Caped Trouble-Maker, swings circles around your friendly neighbourhood Spider-Pig!

Drawn live and in full colour, it’s issue 36 of Simpsons Comic! In this issue, we’ve got the King of Comedy – and his very own sovereign state! Then, we interrupt the clowning around for our regularly scheduled game of cat and mouse. Remember, whatever you do, be sure to try this at home!

Hi-diddley-ho readerinos! Welcome to issue 37 of Simpsons Comics! Kids rule not only in the school in this issue, but the airwaves too! We’ve got a classic whodunnit, whacked-out weather, and a wild ride down the Red River. Not to mention the answer to an age-old question: what do you get with a drunken sailor?

They call themselves the Simpsons Family… and in this issue of Simpsons Comics, they’re about to star in all your favourite sci-fi blockbusters. This super awesome mix of Simpsons stories sees Barlord and Brat the Destroyer save the moon, whilst a Martian menaces the local yokels. Pick up Simpsons Comics #38 for stories which are guaranteed to be out of this world!

Welcome to Simpsons Comics issue 39! In this issue, Marge finds herself on both sides of the law when justice comes to Springfield – from petty crimes to pretty huge fines, Marge Simpson is judge, jury and prisoner. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa discover that no money is mo’ problems!

A comic about comics? How original! In this mint first-printing edition of Simpsons Comics #40, delve into the Android’s Dungeon and be careful with those greasy fingers! You meta believe it when Bart and Milhouse head to work at Boffo Comics, and love and body odour is in the air at the local comic convention!

It’s said that “brevity is the soul of wit” – but I never was that funny! In this issue of Simpsons Comics, Shakespeare takes centre stage – but it’s not what they teach you in school! After a quick ice-cream break in the interval, vigilante justice and Machiavellian criminal masterminds threaten Bart and the brightest of Springfield Elementary!

Is it a bird? Is it a Duff blimp? No! it’s Simpsons Comics #42! In this issue we’ve collected the first two parts of The Best Radioactive Man Event Ever!– with part three coming in next month’s issue! The fate of Springfield hands in the balance, as Bart heads up and atom!

It’s finally here –Simpsons Comics #43! In this issue, we’ve got the epic conclusion of The Best Radioactive Man Event Ever! Then, Springfield’s resident mad scientist is pushed to the Frink, and not even Homer can stop the revenge of the nerds!

Thor has returned to this dimension to find that much has changed! A man claiming to be Heimdall has taken hostage the "Balloon Bunch Day Care" and promises not to hurt anyone if he gets an audience with the Mighty Thor! The only way to prove if this man is the guardian of the Rainbow Bridge or not is to take him to Asgard. Apon their arrival Thor learns his identity. In anger and sadness of the fall of his great home and kingdom Thor throws his hammer Mjolnir into the ruins of Asgard only to, not to his realization, free the Destroyer! With this "god killer" on the loose The Avengers must act quickly with the help of their most powerful member (Thor). The Destroyer is almost invincible! The Avengers must fight with all that is in them to defeat this great foe! But will that be enough?

Finally. The mighty Thor confronts the Dark Gods responsible for the down fall of Asgard and the attack on the Olympian Gods. But the Odinson will soon learn that even the power of a Thunder God may not be enough to prevail against Perrikus, the God of Power incarnate.

The unthinkable has happened. Perrikus, the Dark God of Power, has shattered Mjolnir, one of the most powerful weapons in all the universe. And now, due to the enchantment placed upon him by the mysterious Marnot, only the mortal Jake Olson remains where the mighty Thor once stood. All is lost and the Odinson stands powerless to stop the rising tide of darkness.

This is it! The final battle for the fate of Asgard and the future of mankind. His sacred hammer made whole once more, the God of Thunder with the Lion of Olympus, Hercules, and the unstoppable Destroyer by his side makes an all out attack on the indomitable Dark Gods. The Nine Worlds tremble when gods make war!
At last, the secrets of Marnot are revealed! Who is this mysterious benefactor of the Thunder God's? He who can make even the Mistress of the Underworld, Hela, falter in her step?

The mighty Thor battles one of his oldest and most powerful adversaries, Crusher Creel the Absorbing Man and his super-strong squeeze Titania. But this time the odinson does not fight alone. The Invincible Iron Man fights by his side. Plus, the secrets as to why Thor's hammer has been acting strange of late begin to be revealed in this very issue.

Omnipotent Odin sends the Warriors Three to his son's aid. For Jake Olson lies at death's door and mighty Mjolnir remains magically stuck in the wall. Could this be the work of the sinister Enchanters?
Thor, Odin, and the valiant Warriors Three stand against the mystic might of the Enchanters! Plus, the return of the Prince of Lies!

What on earth could put the fear of God into the Unstoppable Juggernaut? The mighty Thor intends to find out, but first he'll have to stop the earthly avatar of Cyttorak from destroy downtown Manhattan.

The Warriors Three stand side -by-side with mortals and face the legions of evil. Plus, after a little help from the Scarlet Witch the Odinson has discovered the location of his enemies, the Enchanters, and the All-Father. Meanwhile, the Prince of Lies, Loki, conspires with the embodiment of evil, Mephisto.

Thor and Odin are swallowed by the Enchanters’ magical beast. If they do not act with haste, they will be dissolved within the belly of the beast. But what will the warrior gods do when Mjolnir has no effect on the monster?
Thor has fallen! While the Avengers continue their battle against the Destroyer, Thor must contend with Hela, dark mistress of the underworld!
Thor’s alter-ego, Jake, is under the control of a puppet master. And that puppet master is Loki!
Thor makes a terrible discovery when he travels to Asgard to seek the council of the gods.
It’s Thor versus Thanos in a battle for the future!
Thor, Firelord, and the Recorder head to stop Thanos and Mangog. But it may already be too late!
Thor, alongside Firelord and the Recorder, battle Thanos and Mangog!
Freshly infused with energy from newly acquired armaments, Thor engages in a final showdown with Thanos!

Thor returns home to fabled Asgard where the All-Father begins his week long Odin sleep (a hibernating process the King of the Aesir takes once a year to replenish his strength). He soon learns that Lady Sif has been appointed Keeper of the Realms. Meanwhile back on Midgard, Crusher Creel, the Absorbing Man, has learned that the woman he loves, Titania, is dying. He kidnaps Jane Foster to save her life and Jake Olson pays the cost for standing in his way.

The always dangerous Absorbing Man has kidnaped Doctor Jane Foster and gives her the ultimatum...help his dying love, Titania, or else. Can the Thunder God find his ex-girlfriend before it's too late, and what will be the final fate of Titania?

The mighty Thor, with the valiant Warriors Three by his side, faces off against the muscle-bound menace of the Wrecking Crew. Things turn deadly when one of the Odinson's allies is left at death's doorstep.

Hogun the Grim has been mortally wounded. But when Hela, Mistress of the Underworld, comes to claim her prize the Thunder God stands in her way. Meanwhile, the Dark Elf, Malekith plots and schemes from the shadows. And, Thor pays a little visit to the Wrecking Crew for some much needed payback.

Now sharing space in the physical realm with a man named Jake, Thor must deal with the intricacies of mortal life. But when the sea goddess, Sedna, begins an aquatic rampage, the Odinson is called upon to save the day!

Malekith, the Dark Elf, has the Casket of Ancient Winters in his possession and the realms tremble in fear. Meanwhile, Thor and the Avengers continue their desperate mission in space. Plus, the startling return of Beta-Ray Bill!

Can even the Son of Odin stop the machinations of Malekith when the dark elf unleashes the power of the Casket of Ancient Winters upon fabled Asgard? Luckily, his comrades in arms Beta-Ray Bill and the Warriors Three are at his side. But even that might not be enough when the Dark Elf's new ally, one of the Thunder God's deadliest adversaries, makes the scene.

100-page Giant! The Dark Elf, Malekith, has unleashed the icing death of the Casket of Ancient Winters on Asgard and only the God of Thunder can stop him. But first he'll have to get past the indomitable Kurse, a foe whose strength rivals his own. Plus, "To Become an Immortal!" A tale originally presented in Thor (1st Series) #136. Story by Stan Lee. Art by Jack Kirby and Vince Colletta. Thor has brought his beloved before the All-Father so that they may be wed. However, Odin will not see the Prince of Asgard married to a mere mortal. So what does the Omnipotent One do? He turns Jane Foster into an immortal! "The Day the Thunder Failed!" Story by Roy Thomas. Art by John Buscema and Tom Palmer. An epic tale from Thor and Loki's past. "The Kursed Earth...!" Guest-starring Power Pack. Story and art by Walter Simonson. Originally presented in Thor (1st Series ) #. A Secret Wars II tie-in that features the Beyonder resurrecting Kurse and doubling his already considerable strength before sending the behemoth after the Odinson. And finally, The Tales of Asgard backup features "The Meaning of Ragnarok!" and "Aftermath!" Originally presented in Thor (1962-1996 1st Series) #127-128. By Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

issue_title: The Million Dollar Debut of Thor Girl
description: Thor battles a giant robot in the middle of time square. A mysterious new heroine with ties to the Thunder God's past arrives on the scene. Plus, a sinister foe from the future plots the Odinson's death.

The Odinson takes time out to train the Designate, now going by Thor Girl, in the art of combat. Meanwhile, the super-powerful Gladiator, of the Shi'ar Imperial Guard, scours the city in search of Thor. When he does find the Thunder God what follows is anything but pretty. Plus, Ulik, the strongest of all trolls, plots and schemes from the shadows.
In a dark future in which Thor is considered responsible for Zarko sends Gladiator back to the present in order to kill Thor. future Odin wakes from his Odinsleep to defeat Ulik.
Loki and Karnilla take advantage of the fact that Odin has turned Thor into a mortal.

The Watcher pays an ominous visit to Odin and brings dire news of a future yet to come. Meanwhile, Thor and Lady Sif are locked in deadly combat with the unstoppable Destroyer. Worse yet, the mighty Thunder God can not raise a hand in his own defense for fear of injuring the essence which fuels his silent adversary, Tarene the Designate. Plus, the return of Asgard's greatest enemy!

Can Odin sit idly by while his favored son meets his end at the hands of his own creation, the Destroyer? Maybe the Thunder God doesn't need daddy's help. Not when the Enchantress is here to lend a hand. That's right, the Enchantress. Plus, the greatest threat the Golden Realm has ever faced returns to this plane of existence.

The fiery titan, Surtur, has returned and the realms quake in fear. For last time this firey giant attempted to conquer the realms it took the combined might of Thor, all the heroes of Earth, the warriors of Asgard and Valhalla, Beta Ray Bill, Loki, and the ultimate sacrifice by the All-Father himself to defeat him.
With his control over Mjolnir on the fritz, Thor faces death by drowning in his battle against Sedna! Plus, an appearance by Sub-Mariner!

They say "history has a way of repeating itself." The war with the fire titan known as Surtur comes crashing to its ultimate conclusion with a finish you'll have to see to believe. Needless to say, the landscape of the Nine Worlds will never be the same again as one god is forced to make the ultimate sacrifice.

To defeat the ultimate evil, Odin, Lord of Asgard, made the ultimate sacrifice. Now, Thor and his allies are left to pick up the pieces left in the wake of the war with Surtur. Most important of all, the throne of Asgard sits empty. Plus, the return of Skurge the Executioner.

Before Thor, the Viking God of Thunder, can look to the future, he must first make peace and bring about closure with his mortal counterpart, Jake Olson. Meanwhile, the Dark Gods await the coming of Desak the God Killer.

Thor Girl engages one of the deadliest warriors in all the realms - Skurge the Executioner. Meanwhile, the Odinson ascends to the throne of Asgard. There's a new king and his name is Thor, Lord of Asgard! Plus, the Dark Gods meet with their ultimate fate at the hands of Desak the God Killer.

In this all silent issue, the mighty Thor is now Lord of Asgard, but it is a somber day indeed. The All-Father, Odin, sacrificed himself in battle against the fire god Surtur in order to save the realms from total destruction. This beautifully illustrated issue shows the toll Odin's death has taken on his subjects and enemies alike and how he affected their lives. But more importantly, the God of Thunder is shown to finally accept his role and takes up his father's crown.
The burden of rule begins to weigh heavy on the Odinson's soul. Meanwhile, Baldur the Brave quests for a fabled Chest of Strength. And, the Lord of Asgard receives council from a follow Sky Father.

issue_title: By Fire Born Part I of V
description: Tarene continues her succession as protector of the realm of Midgard in the guise of Thor Girl. But, will it be a short reign as she comes into fatal contact with one of the Thunder God's deadliest enemies. Meanwhile, Amora the Enchantress arrives in Asgard.

issue_title: By Fire Born Part II of V
description: While the Lord of Asgard battles Frost Giants in Asgard, the unthinkable has happened back on Midgard. The Grey Gargoyle has murdered Tarene and seemingly stolen her immortality. Only Jake Olson can save the Designate now, but he no longer possesses the power of the Thunder God, or does he. Plus, the arrival of an extremely powerful force could mean the end of everyone.

issue_title: By Fire Born Part III of V
description: Thor and the warriors of Asgard war with the Frost Giants in Asgard. But can the Aesir prevail against the frosty behemoths when the Thunder God's power has been cut in half? Meanwhile, Jake Olson, endowed with the power of the Thunder God, is confronted by not only Desak, a powerful warrior form another world who seeks the Odinson's death, but also the Grey Gargoyle, the villain who has stolen the Designate's immortality.

issue_title: By Fire Born, Part IV of V

description: It's bad enough a popular radio D.J. is maligning Thor on the airwaves. Things get much worse when Mjolnir itself tries to kill the man...

issue_title: By Fire Born, Part V of V
description: Take a look back at the way things were and how they've become the way they are today when the Spirit of the Jewel recalls the swirling mass of events, the moments of causality, and the pinpoints of destiny in Asgard and on Earth!

The mighty Thor, now the undisputed Lord of Asgard, has made a decision to get more involved in the affairs of mortals. Asgard, the fabled city of the Norse Gods, floats above New York City, and the US government is not happy about. The Amazing Spider-Man attempts to council a god, but an attack from below only proves Thor's point that the time has come for immortals to once again guide their mortal brethren to enlightenment.

The time of "The Reigning" has begun. The Lord of the Aesir has brought forth Asgard, home of the Norse Gods, to guide mortal man to a better future. But first take a look at time long since past when the Thunderer was but a young godling still learning the ways of mortal man. Plus, meet Thialf, the orphaned boy who would be taken in by the gods.

The Dark Gods have returned to Asgard to conquer! This time they will find the task a much more difficult one as it is now Thor the mighty Thunder God who rules here. But who is the true mastermind behind their attack? The answer does not sit well with the new Lord of Asgard.

Imagine a world where men can walk on walls, a little girl can walk through walls, some can read minds, and gods walk the earth. Dan Jurgens and Joe Bennett take a look at what it means to have faith in the Marvel Universe.

The Lord of Asgard addresses the United Nations, Loki and Amora the Enchantress find that they may have finally achieved their life's long dreams, and Zarrko the Tomorrow Man predicts bad tidings to come. Plus, the most unexpected outcome to a confrontation between Thor and the Absorbing Man you could ever imagine.

Thor has come to Midgard to offer his godly guidance, but not everyone is on board with what the Thunder God has to offer. One man is willing to do anything to discredit the Thunderer. Even stage his own death.

Dan Jurgens and his cadre of talent artist bring you a tale of imagination as told by Volstagg the Stout. In this unique issue each every turn of the page reveals a 2-page spread, each rendered by a different artist.

After taking on the role as ruler of Asgard, Thor has relocated his legendary home to float directly over New York City. But how will the citizens of the world -- including Thor's former allies in the Avengers -- react when a host of self-styled Gods decides to intercede in the affairs of man?

issue_title: The Substance of Things Hoped For
description: The year is 2026 A.D. A homeless teenager makes a startling discovery - the long lost magical Hammer of Thor! Is that crazy old man going on and on really the Odinson? Is that shady looking man in the trench coat really Loki, the Lord of Lies? D.J. intends to find out.

The mysterious Marnot comes to the Odinson with a boon. Plus, Jake Olson is presented with a medal to honor his bravery by none other then the Sentinel of Liberty himself, Captain America. Plus, the mighty Thor seeks the aid of the Lion of Olympus, but not before Hercules bestows the gift of battle on his friend.

Jake Olson, a valiant young man considered by many to be the best EMT in the city, was once the earthly avatar of the God of Thunder. Even though he no longer possesses the power of a god, Jake is still a force for good and he proves everyday by helping his fellow man. Meanwhile, Thor goes on a mystical sojourn where a clandestine meeting with the All-Father will teach him more about the Odin Force and his place in the universe.

The Lord of Asgard attends a meeting with his fellow Sky Fathers: Zeus, Osiris, Yu-Huang, Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva. Here he will put through a test to see if he is worthy of taking his father's seat at the table. Meanwhile, Volstagg has been appointed a most sacred task - the protection of Tarene the Designate. She who is key to the unification of the universe. He'll find it a task easier said than done.
Thor continues to try and find the wisdom his father used to rule the Golden Realm. Meanwhile, what is Zarrko the Tomorrow Man up to and what secrets does he know about the Odinson's future?

One man vows to move heaven and earth to get his son, a devout Thor fan, to college. As fate would have it, fortune does not smile upon him. But when he bares witness to divine intervention, Lars must rethink his stance on faith.

Thor, Lord of Asgard, is using the vast power at his command to heal the sick and feed the hungry. As his influence over the world of mortals increases so does the number of his followers. Thorist, once thought of as nothing more than a cult, have grown into legion and the religion of Asgardianism is growing everyday. So where does the Prince of Lies, Loki fit into all this? Read on and find out.
Has Thor finally crosses a line. When the Lord of Asgard uses the Odin Force to resurrect a small child the world and other pantheon lords look on in horror and dismay.
In the aftermath of last issues events, more and more people are turning against Thor. America declares war on Asgard! Could this be the beginning of the end predicted by Zarrko the Tomorrow Man?

The US government has declared all out war on Asgard. They tried to murder the Thunder God with a nuclear explosion and they've invaded the scared halls of the Golden Realm with their stormtroopers. To say that the Lord of Asgard is displease would be an understatement. Featuring the death of a major character and Thor's fall from grace.

The time of "The Reigning" is upon mankind. Seventeen years ago New York City and Asgard was destroyed as a result of war between man and god. Now in the year 2020, Thor and his royal consorts rule the world and intend to lead mankind into the future. Whether they like it or not.
It is many years since the Aesir took control of Midgard. Now Earth shall be reconfigured to meet the vision of Thor, Lord of Asgard. Plus, a shocking last page you have to see to believe.

Thor and Hercules have arrived on fabled Mount Olympus only to find the home of the Olympian Gods ravaged. But even worse is the news they are met with from Lord Zeus himself. For it was the Asgardians who attacked Olympus. Refusing to believe such heresy, Thor vows to find the true culprits behind the fall of Asgard and Olympus.

The Aesir, the fabled Norse Gods, now rule mankind. But there are those who will ever oppose them. Plus, Thor reveals his master plan for his mortal subjects. Featuring the daughter of the Scarlet Witch. And introducing Magni, the son of Thor.
Thiafi learns some hard truths about his king. Truths that may cause him to rethink his stance on things. Plus, Magni meets Jordah's mother.

In light of recent revelations, Thiafi's faith in the Lord of Asgard, and his beloved friend, Thor has been shaken. Plus, Thor's own son, Magni, learns some hard truths of his own about how mortal man feels about the Aesir's rule.

Take a look back at the year 2020 and bare witness to the last stand of the heroes of Earth. Captain America, Vison, Doctor Strange, Hulk, Thing, and Wolverine mount one final, albeit, desperate assault in an attempt to topple Thor's rule.

Led by the daughter of the Scarlet Witch, mankind makes it final attempt to dethrone the Lord of Asgard. And they just might succeed to for Thiafi, Thor's closest friend and confidant has decided that the Odinson is no longer fit to rule. Is this the end of "The Reigning?"

Magni, the son of Thor, discovers the missing hammer, Mjolnir. Proving himself worthy the youthful god raises one of the most powerful weapons in the universe in triumph. And, somewhere deep in space...Desak, the Destroyer of Gods, awakens.
The climax of Thor's reign as the ruler of Asgard begins NOW! The action heats up and the heavens tremble as all the Thunder God has built comes to ruins, and those closest to Thor betray him!
Only one can wield Mjolnir, the mighty mystic Uru hammer. Will it be Thor, or his son Magni? And must the son kill the father in order to restore peace on Earth?
Will the devastating attack of Desak, Destroyer of Gods, on the empire Thor has built unite the Odinson and his son, Magni? Who will wield the unstoppable hammer, Mjolnir?

Confronted by his son Magni to lift Mjolnir, and attacked by Desak, Thor finally realizes the error of his rule over Earth and sees Loki once more for what he is, The Trickster. With the help of Tarene the Lord of Asgard will look for a way to atone and set things right.

issue_title: . . . And the Home of the Brave!
description: When Thor attempts to return to Asgard he finds his passage mystically blocked. But he does not have long to contemplate this as an agent of the Dark Gods descends upon the helpless mortals under his protection. But even with the Amazing Spider-Man by his side, can the Thunder God prevail against this new foe?

RAGNAROK PART 1

It's the beginning of the end of the world for the Gods of Asgard, and only Thor and his Avengers allies might be able to stave off that fate- but does the God of Thunder even want to? Thor- Disassembled starts here!

In the land of the dwarfs, Odin and his brothers formed the earth as gods. After forming the Earth, Odin visits three dwarfish craftsmen to make him a weapon. They make Mjolnir a war hammer out of parts of the sun. Loki came into Asgard when Odin killed his real father and took Loki in as an orphan. Odin always favored Thor over Loki and this made Loki jealous. Odin gives Thor Mjolnir and this enrages Loki. Wanting to get a weapon equal to Mjolnir, Loki sets out to search for the mold which was used to make Mjolnir.

After the three craftsmen dwarfs died, they were honored by the gods and put to rest in a tomb. Thor and a few friends: Hogun, Volstagg, Fandral, Sif, Baldur, and Amora head for the tomb to pay their respects. As they are mourning their deaths, they are attacked by Loki and a few of his goons (Hyrm, Ulik "The Invincible", and Fenris "The Wolf"). During the fight, Loki's crew knocks down a stone pillar and it strikes both Thor and Amora "The Enchantress" to the ground. Amora is feared to be dead and Thor is dazed. He staggers to his feet only to be met by Hyrm and they begin to battle. After a short period of time, Hyrm and Thor's hammers strike each other which causes an explosion. Mjolnir is broken. He shouts, "Avengers Assemble!". Back in Midgard--Earth--Captain America and Iron Man are busy saving people from a burning building when they get the call...

RAGNAROK PART 2

The immortal city of Asgard suddenly seems quite mortal, as Captain America, Iron Man, and Thor discover. The God of Thunder must lead what is left of the Asgardians into their (likely) final battle!

Hearing Thor's call, Captain America and Iron Man come to his aid in Asgard "home of the gods". Walking through a battlefield they survey the dead and try to figure out what happened before they arrived. How does Thor not know? Hmm... Sifting through some of the rubble Captain America notices that there's a young boy trapped under a pile of wood. He frees the rubble and swaddles the kid. They begin questioning him as to what happened on the battlefield. Immediately Thor assumes that it was the work of trolls but the kid corrects them--It was Loki and his goons.

Just as the kid advises them of their doing another battle ensues with Loki and his crew. Thor calls Loki out and challenges him to a one-on-one. Loki declines and sends Ulik and Fenris after them. Captain gets bit by Ulik during the fight. Loki and friends retreat after a long battle.

Afterwards Thor, Iron Man, and Captain America head for town. They arrive and find themselves in the middle of a funeral for a fallen soldier in the battle. The funeral is for Balder, Thor's brother. Thor is upset and calls for his mother Frigga. Thor gives a motivating speech for all those that still remain in his service, he seeks revenge for all of the injustice.

RAGNAROK PART 3

Ragnarok appears to have come for the gods of Asgard, but will Thor be their savior, or its architect? In search of new wisdom, the Thunder God must repeat the ordeals of Odin, and the price may be too terrible for even an immortal to pay!

Volstagg, Hogun, and Fandral come into Alfheim--home of the light elves--looking for safe refuge from battle carrying the injured Sif. They are greeted by a few elves and they rush to their aid. As soon as they meet up, they look to the sky to see Naglfar--the ghost ship approaching. They fear their doom.

In the present day, Volstagg, crumbles a statue to find Thor resting and recovering. Thor immediately notices that there is something different about Volstagg. Volstagg is skinny, he's as trim as a goat! Volstagg reports to Thor, who begins to believe that he was the last surviving of his kind. Volstagg tells of the last two battles and of the falling of all of his friends (Sif, Hogun, Baldur, and Fandral).

Thor and Volstagg begin to travel back to the battlegrounds to survey the area. On their journey back, they begin to recruit other survivors, orphans, and volunteers to their cause. After making it back to the main battlegrounds, Thor begins to recognize some of the fallen. Specifically, Kurse and Vidar--his brother. As they are tending to the wounded they are attacked by Fenris the wolf. During the fight, they are joined by Valkyrie "Defender of the Earth". Shortly after joining the battle, Valkyrie is struck down and killed. Once she was vanquished, another foe joined in the festivities--Durok "the Demolisher". He gets stabbed by Sif's sword (Dragonfang) at the same time Thor is launching Fenris with his fists. Thor hurrys over to finish off Durok and then begins to take on Fenris for a third time when he is joined by Beta-Ray Bill...

RAGNAROK PART 4

Spearheading the Midland forces is the Band of the Hawk, a legendary cadre of elite mercenaries led by the charismatic Griffith and with the fearless Guts as its berserker champion.

Captain Kirk is buried and wakes up in unfamiliar territory.
Captain Kirk finds he is lost in time, having gone back hundreds of years before his crew even visited this planet. Somehow he has to beat time itself with absolutely nothing technological.

Without warning, the Enterprise is sent on a top-secret mission: ferrying a Vulcan diplomat who is authorized to countermand any of Kirk's orders.

Part 2 of 3. Kirk's actions have offended an alien race and threatened interstellar peace. Only Spock's old rival, Ambassador Stonn, may be able to undo the damage before the Romulans take advantage of a volatile situation.

Part 3 of 3. Stonn's deception puts delicate negotiations in jeopardy while, on the planet 'Gi, Spock attempts to reason with Stonn's rebellious daughter, whose actions have placed her and Spock in mortal danger.

description: A Wolf in Cheap Clothing, Part 1 of 4. The Klingon Empire is poised to enter an expansionist phase, threatening the shaky new peace with the Federation, and Starfleet sends its two best ships - the Enterprise and the Excelsior - to learn the truth.

issue_title: A Wolf...In Cheap Clothing Part Two
description: A Wolf in Cheap Clothing, Part 2 of 4. Finding the situation even more volatile than Starfleet had believed, Kirk pulls out the landing party from Zantak Prime.

issue_title: A Wolf...In Cheap Clothing Part Three

issue_title: A Wolf...In Cheap Clothing The Conclusion!
description: A Wolf in Cheap Clothing, Part 4 of 4. Kirk learns that a sacred relic of the Klingon people has been stolen - one that could cause the downfall of the Klingon High Council and plunge the Empire into anarchy.

Star-Crossed, Part 2 of 3. Before taking command of the Starship Enterprise, Kirk visits Carol Marcus and is shocked to meet their infant son.

Star-Crossed, Part 3 of 3. At the end of Kirk's first 5-year mission aboard the Starship Enterprise, Starfleet's Intrawarp Development Project offers the promise of a revolution in spaceflight. Kirk, Spock and Commander Gary Mitchell visit a world where any infraction of the law is punishable by imprisonment.
Disabled by Romulans, the Starship Enterprise is left to the 'tender' mercies of a new threat that has already attacked Federation outposts along the Neutral Zone.

The Chosen, Part 1 of 3. The Enterprise intercepts a desperate distress call from a Klingon outpost. Arriving too late, Kirk finds the outpost wiped out, and the chilling evidence that Starfleet weapons were behind the destruction.

The attack echoes a recent assault on a Klingon outpost, and all evidence points to the Romulans. Kirk is ordered to work alongside a civilian specialist to learn the truth...but the answers may prove lethal.
Part 3 of 4. Sweeney, the most dangerous mercenary in the universe, has set up an auction between the Klingons and the Nasgul...with the kidnapped Kirk, Spock and Blaise as the prize.

Final issue. The Chosen, Part 3 of 3. Kirk must convince the Romulans and the Klingons to work with him in order to prevent the cataclysm that will surely follow if they don't put aside their mutual distrust.
